content: SGLT2 inhibitors are typically advised for patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who also have type 2 diabetes (T2D) and either significant albuminuria or a confirmed reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). These medications have demonstrated clinical benefits even in the later stages of CKD. However, their glucose-lowering efficacy becomes less pronounced when the eGFR falls below 45 mL/min/1.73 m². Despite this, evidence suggests that SGLT2 inhibitors continue to provide cardiovascular and renal protective effects in patients with eGFR levels as low as 20 mL/min/1.73 m².
